channel.title: WesCastle Blog
channel.description: Field notes from offensive security engagements, developer tooling, and infrastructure ownership. By Wes Hardcastle.

item.title: Your Badge Reader Trusts Me More Than It Trusts You
item.description: A field-notes account of cloning access-control badges on physical pentests — 125 kHz prox cards, a $50 Proxmark, why RFID access control is mostly theater, and the handful of controls that actually raise the cost of the attack.

item.title: I Got Into Your Datacenter With a Clipboard
item.description: A field-notes account of physical penetration testing — clipboards, business-casual pretexts, $40 of hardware, wireless drop boxes in open Ethernet ports, and the part nobody talks about: leaving every site on good terms.

item.title: FourDollarVPN — A $4/month WireGuard VPN in One Command
item.description: FourDollarVPN spins up a personal WireGuard VPN on DigitalOcean in about 90 seconds, for about $4 a month. One command, no config files, no commercial provider you have to take at their word.

item.title: What Developers Actually Own When Every Tool Is Someone Else's Platform
item.description: Your code is on GitHub. Your DNS is on Cloudflare. Your email is on Google. Your deployments are on Vercel. What do you actually own? Less than you think.

item.title: ForkOff: Open-Source GitHub Backup Tool That Runs While You Sleep
item.description: GitHub can suspend your account without warning. ForkOff is a free, open-source tool that mirrors all your repos locally every day — so it doesn't matter if they do.
